premises.text: Online fashion lacks personalization because shoppers cannot see how clothes fit on bodies unlike standard models
premises.evidence_span: What's missing in online fashion shopping is personalization

premises.text: Shoppers create a personal body model from just brand-and-size answers they already wear well
premises.evidence_span: Creating a model is as simple as answering just two basic questions

premises.text: Browser-based true-to-size 3D fitting/styling lets shoppers try sizes and full outfits on their model without special hardware
premises.evidence_span: This is true to size. That means she can try on each sizes one by one and really see how each size would fit

premises.text: Digitizing designer collections at scale and offering them to retailers via API with pay-as-you-go pricing
premises.evidence_span: we offer this collection to the retailers who carry these designers using our API

premises.text: Retailers gain size and style analytics from consumer try-ons to optimize operations
premises.evidence_span: They get access to all the sizes from the consumers

value.text: Shoppers try clothes online on a personal true-to-size model so more fashion sales can move online
value.evidence_span: What if you can create your own model and try on clothes on that model?

secondary_value.text: Retailers get increased sales, reduced returns, and new fit analytics
secondary_value.evidence_span: They get increased sales, reduced returns, and they get access to this amazing data

causal_links.evidence_span: People still don't know how clothes fit when they're buying online
trying on clothes is as simple as dragging and dropping on the model
the retailers have no upfront costs. They pay us as they go

notes: Fit uncertainty and standard-model display folded as one problem (§4.1.6). Drag/zoom/rotate, side-by-side sizes, full-outfit styling, and no-hardware browser delivery folded as cascade of one true-to-size fitting room (§4.1.7). Mass-customization/Holy Grail vision not coded as a premise (§4.1.4). Designer logos and Indian-retailer announcement treated as traction (§4.2). Three domains—anti-template: retailer API economics separately revisable from consumer fitting UX.
